scenes.text: It's the night of March 8th, 1862, and a warship is burning in front of you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: She is the USS Congress, a frigate that was the pride of the fleet this morning.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: One enemy ship did this, in a single afternoon.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: It destroyed two warships and killed more than two hundred sailors.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: Every cannonball the fleet fired at it just bounced off.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: Tomorrow morning, it comes back to finish the job.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: The only thing in its way is you: Lieutenant Dana Greene, barely out of the Naval Academy.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: Your ship is brand new, half finished, and it nearly sank on the way here.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: By the end, you'll know how four hours tomorrow make every navy on Earth obsolete.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: And why neither ship could actually win.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: But first: how does one ship beat a whole fleet?
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: Go back one year, to the navy yard at Norfolk, Virginia.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: The Confederacy has almost no navy.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: But it does have the burned hull of a Union frigate: the Merrimack.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: So its engineers cut her down to the waterline, and build an iron barn on top.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: The walls are four inches of iron, over two feet of wood.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: And the walls slope.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: So a cannonball doesn't punch through: it skips off, like a stone off a pond.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: The iron plates arrive so slowly that she takes nearly a year to finish.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: They rename her the CSS Virginia, and bolt an iron beak to her bow.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: She is slow, and she needs more than half an hour just to turn around.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: Her guns cannot be raised, so they only reach about a mile.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: One officer watching the work tells her engineer: she will prove your coffin.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: In March 1862, her new captain arrives: Flag Officer Franklin Buchanan.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: He does not plan a trial run. He tells his engineer: I am going to ram the Cumberland.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: I am going to ram the Cumberland.

scenes.bgIdea: stone dry dock at the Gosport Navy Yard, Norfolk, Virginia, 1861: the cut-down hull of a steam frigate being covered with a sloping iron casemate, wooden scaffolding, stacks of iron plates, a crane

scenes.text: March 8th, 1862. Buchanan steams out toward the Union's wooden fleet.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: He tells his crew that the Confederacy expects every man to do his duty.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: The Confederacy expects every man to do his duty.

scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: On the USS Cumberland, the sailors' washing is still drying in the rigging.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: open gun deck of the wooden Union sloop-of-war USS Cumberland at anchor, March 1862: row of black cannons on carriages, masts and rigging with sailors' washing drying on lines, calm bay, morning light

scenes.text: Then her gunners fire everything they have.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: open gun deck of the wooden Union sloop-of-war USS Cumberland at anchor, March 1862: row of black cannons on carriages, masts and rigging with sailors' washing drying on lines, calm bay, morning light

scenes.text: The shells hit the sloping iron, and burst harmlessly in the air.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: open gun deck of the wooden Union sloop-of-war USS Cumberland at anchor, March 1862: row of black cannons on carriages, masts and rigging with sailors' washing drying on lines, calm bay, morning light

scenes.text: Buchanan shouts across the water: do you surrender?
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: The answer from the Cumberland is one word: never.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: open gun deck of the wooden Union sloop-of-war USS Cumberland at anchor, March 1862: row of black cannons on carriages, masts and rigging with sailors' washing drying on lines, calm bay, morning light

scenes.text: So he rams her, below the waterline.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: The sinking ship nearly drags the Virginia down with her.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: Then the iron beak snaps off, and stays in the wound. Remember that beak.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: The Cumberland keeps firing for forty minutes, until she is under water.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: open gun deck of the wooden Union sloop-of-war USS Cumberland at anchor, March 1862: row of black cannons on carriages, masts and rigging with sailors' washing drying on lines, calm bay, morning light

scenes.text: Next, the Congress runs aground, and raises a white flag.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: Buchanan knows that ship: his own brother is an officer on board.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: Then rifle fire from the shore hits Buchanan himself.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: As he is carried below, he orders the Congress set on fire.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: His gunners heat cannonballs red in the furnaces, and fire them into her.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: A third frigate, the Minnesota, is stuck on a sandbank nearby.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: But the Virginia sits twenty-three feet deep, and cannot get close enough to kill her.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: So she anchors for the night. The Minnesota can wait until morning.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: It stays the US Navy's worst day for almost eighty years, until Pearl Harbor.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: open gun deck of the wooden Union sloop-of-war USS Cumberland at anchor, March 1862: row of black cannons on carriages, masts and rigging with sailors' washing drying on lines, calm bay, morning light

scenes.text: The Union's answer comes from a Swedish-born engineer in New York: John Ericsson.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: His design has no masts, no sails, and almost no ship.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It is a flat iron raft, with one spinning iron tower in the middle.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: IRON RAFT + ONE SPINNING GUN TOWER

scenes.text: Two giant guns sit in a turret that turns to aim, so the ship doesn't have to.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The turret wall is eight layers of iron, each an inch thick.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The captain steers from a small iron box near the bow, looking out through a one-inch slit.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember that slit.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The Navy is not convinced: if it fails, Ericsson must pay back every dollar.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He builds it in about a hundred days.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Critics call it Ericsson's folly, and a cheesebox on a raft.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Its real name is the USS Monitor.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Her captain, John Worden, volunteered for the job before the keel was even laid.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor by day, 1862: riveted iron plates, the round riveted gun turret with two gun ports, a small square iron pilot house near the bow, grey sky and open water

scenes.text: You join her as second in command, with a crew of volunteers.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor by day, 1862: riveted iron plates, the round riveted gun turret with two gun ports, a small square iron pilot house near the bow, grey sky and open water

scenes.text: There is no time for trial runs. She goes to sea with nothing finished.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor by day, 1862: riveted iron plates, the round riveted gun turret with two gun ports, a small square iron pilot house near the bow, grey sky and open water

scenes.text: Off the coast, a gale rolls the sea right over her deck.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor by day, 1862: riveted iron plates, the round riveted gun turret with two gun ports, a small square iron pilot house near the bow, grey sky and open water

scenes.text: Water pours down the air pipes, and the fans that feed the engine room stop.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor by day, 1862: riveted iron plates, the round riveted gun turret with two gun ports, a small square iron pilot house near the bow, grey sky and open water

scenes.text: Below, the engineers pass out in the fumes.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor by day, 1862: riveted iron plates, the round riveted gun turret with two gun ports, a small square iron pilot house near the bow, grey sky and open water

scenes.text: The crew drags them up into the air, and the ship stays afloat. Barely.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor by day, 1862: riveted iron plates, the round riveted gun turret with two gun ports, a small square iron pilot house near the bow, grey sky and open water

scenes.text: You arrive a few hours too late, with the Congress still burning.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: In the night, her powder magazine explodes.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: Nobody on your ship sleeps tonight.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor at night, March 1862: riveted iron plates, the round gun turret rising behind, a wooden sailing frigate burning on the dark horizon, orange glow on calm water

scenes.text: Sunday morning in Washington, the cabinet meets in a panic.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Cabinet Room of the White House, 1862: long table with green cloth and papers, leather chairs, wall maps, gas chandelier, tall windows looking out toward the Potomac River

scenes.text: The Secretary of War, Edwin Stanton, does most of the talking.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Cabinet Room of the White House, 1862: long table with green cloth and papers, leather chairs, wall maps, gas chandelier, tall windows looking out toward the Potomac River

scenes.text: He predicts the Virginia will soon put a cannonball into this very room.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Cabinet Room of the White House, 1862: long table with green cloth and papers, leather chairs, wall maps, gas chandelier, tall windows looking out toward the Potomac River

scenes.text: She can't. Remember the twenty-three feet? That is far too deep for the river.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Cabinet Room of the White House, 1862: long table with green cloth and papers, leather chairs, wall maps, gas chandelier, tall windows looking out toward the Potomac River

scenes.text: But nobody in that room is sure, and nobody there has ever seen your ship.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: the Cabinet Room of the White House, 1862: long table with green cloth and papers, leather chairs, wall maps, gas chandelier, tall windows looking out toward the Potomac River

scenes.text: At eight in the morning, the Virginia comes back for a stranded frigate, the Minnesota.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Out from behind the frigate slides a barrel lid with a cheesebox on top.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your captain's plan is simple: steam in a circle, and fire each time the circle touches her.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: An engineer turns the turret. You aim, and you fire every shot yourself.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A solid iron ball, eleven inches wide, hits the Virginia.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It dents her. That's all.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Then a hundred-and-fifty-pound shell hits your turret, square on.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It leaves a dent two and a half inches deep, and stuns two men.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Not one bolt comes loose.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: At one point your captain crawls out onto the deck, under rifle fire, to inspect a hit.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He crawls back in through a gun port with good news.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He tells the crew: the Merrimac could not sink us if we let her pound us for a month.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: The Merrimac could not sink us if we let her pound us for a month.

scenes.text: The men cheer.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: For about four hours the two ships circle, sometimes close enough to touch.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So why can't either one win? Two reasons, and both are a little embarrassing.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Reason one: your guns are a new size, and the Navy is afraid they will burst.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So you are ordered to load no more than fifteen pounds of powder.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: ORDER: 15 POUNDS OF POWDER PER SHOT

scenes.text: Later, the same guns safely fire double that. Today, you'll never know.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Reason two: the Virginia came here to kill wooden ships.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: So she carries exploding shells, and none of the solid shot that breaks iron.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: And her ram? Still stuck in the Cumberland, at the bottom of the bay.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: Both ships brought the wrong weapons to the first ironclad duel in history.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: One Confederate gunnery officer stops firing altogether.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: He says he'd do as much damage by snapping his thumb at you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: Meanwhile, the speaking tube to your captain fails.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So his orders arrive on foot, carried by the paymaster and a clerk.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It works about as well as it sounds.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And the turret is so hard to stop that you fire while it is still spinning.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Then, through the gun port, you watch the Virginia run hard aground on a sandbar.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Her engineers tie down the safety valves, and burn anything that burns.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: She drags herself free, and charges straight at you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: gun deck inside the sloping iron casemate of the Confederate ironclad CSS Virginia, 1862: slanted timber-and-iron walls, heavy cannons on carriages at square ports, lanterns, low beams, smoke

scenes.text: She hits you amidships. Without her beak, it is only a shove.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And her own carpenter reports a new leak in her bow.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Around noon, the two ships pass twenty yards apart.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The Virginia's stern gun fires straight into the Monitor's pilot house.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your captain was looking through the slit. He is blinded.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small captain's cabin below deck on the ironclad USS Monitor, 1862: wood-panelled walls, a narrow sofa, a small desk, an oil lamp, a round deck light in the low ceiling

scenes.text: You help him to his cabin, and the ship is yours.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small captain's cabin below deck on the ironclad USS Monitor, 1862: wood-panelled walls, a narrow sofa, a small desk, an oil lamp, a round deck light in the low ceiling

scenes.text: For a few minutes, the Monitor drifts out of the fight.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The Virginia's officers decide not to risk the shallows again, and turn for home.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You chase her, and fire one last shot.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By half past twelve, it is over. Both sides announce that they won.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The Virginia goes home for solid shot and a new ram. The two ships never fight again.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Later, Worden asks only one thing: have I saved the Minnesota?
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small captain's cabin below deck on the ironclad USS Monitor, 1862: wood-panelled walls, a narrow sofa, a small desk, an oil lamp, a round deck light in the low ceiling

scenes.text: Told yes, he says he doesn't care what becomes of him.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small captain's cabin below deck on the ironclad USS Monitor, 1862: wood-panelled walls, a narrow sofa, a small desk, an oil lamp, a round deck light in the low ceiling

scenes.text: He recovers, and dies an admiral, thirty-five years later.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small captain's cabin below deck on the ironclad USS Monitor, 1862: wood-panelled walls, a narrow sofa, a small desk, an oil lamp, a round deck light in the low ceiling

scenes.text: Weeks later, President Lincoln comes aboard to thank the crew in person.

scenes.text: The Navy's assistant secretary admits he never fully believed in armored ships until this fight.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: flat iron deck of the ironclad USS Monitor by day, 1862: riveted iron plates, the round riveted gun turret with two gun ports, a small square iron pilot house near the bow, grey sky and open water

scenes.text: The real damage lands three thousand miles away, in London.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: newspaper office in London, 1862: iron hand printing press, compositors' type cases, tall writing desks with quill pens and inkwells, gas lamps, stacks of printed sheets, fog at the window

scenes.text: The Times counts a hundred and forty-nine first-class warships in the Royal Navy. After this fight, it says, there are two.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: newspaper office in London, 1862: iron hand printing press, compositors' type cases, tall writing desks with quill pens and inkwells, gas lamps, stacks of printed sheets, fog at the window

scenes.text: That is an exaggeration. But every admiral on Earth gets the point.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: newspaper office in London, 1862: iron hand printing press, compositors' type cases, tall writing desks with quill pens and inkwells, gas lamps, stacks of printed sheets, fog at the window

scenes.text: The Union alone builds more than sixty ships on the Monitor's plan.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The two originals don't survive the year.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In May, the Virginia's own crew blows her up, to keep her from capture.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: On the last night of December, the Monitor sinks in a storm off Cape Hatteras.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Sixteen of her men go down with her.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Her turret was raised in 2002. You can stand next to it today, in Newport News, Virginia.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And nearly every big-gun warship built since carries the same idea: a gun that turns.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So who really won, if neither ship could hurt the other? Tell me below.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.title: THE 4 HOURS THAT MADE EVERY NAVY OBSOLETE

titleOptions: Why Two Ships That Couldn't Hurt Each Other Changed War Forever
The Day Wooden Warships Died (Hampton Roads, 1862)
Monitor vs. Virginia: The Draw That Sank Every Navy
meta.thumbnail: The round Monitor turret and the sloped Virginia casemate firing point-blank, cannonballs bouncing off both; text: 'NOBODY WON'
meta.description:
On March 8, 1862, one Confederate ironclad wrecked a Union fleet in an afternoon. The next morning it met a ship built in about 100 days, and the four-hour draw that followed made every wooden navy obsolete.

A comedic dramatization of documented history.
